subject: Mutual Pathfinder MAP — success criteria, exit gates & eval tests
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medisphere.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Pathfinder MAP — success criteria, exit gates & eval tests

Hi Elena — great meeting earlier. As promised, I sketched a short Mutual Action Plan focused on how Medisphere will evaluate Redwood and what success looks like from both sides. I attached a working MAP (mutual_pathfinder_MAP_v1.xlsx). High level below — please flag anything missing.

Goal: Run a 4-week evaluation of Redwood hosted inference for document-processing workloads (clinical note summarization) and agree go/no-go by end of pilot.

Key success criteria (pass = green):
- Latency: median 95th-percentile token latency <= 120ms for 1–2 concurrent user flows.
- Throughput: sustain 60 qps steady-state for batched job runs with <2% error rate.
- Accuracy/Quality: ROUGE-L improvement compared to baseline >= 7 points on our sampled prompt set (see tab: "eval-prompts").
- Cost: projected per-1M-token inference cost <= $X (we'll fill with procurement team).
- Security: credentials + network controls validated, SOC2 evidence provided.

Acceptance tests / exit gates (must all be green for go):
- Smoke: end-to-end demo with representative payloads (week 1).
- Regression: run 2000 sample prompts through current model and baseline; quality delta measured and documented (week 2).
- Load: controlled load test to 60 qps with KV/cache warmed (week 3).
- Compliance: share SOC2 summary and confirm agreed retention policy and audit logs (week 1–2).

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (kickoff): access, ingest sample dataset, finalize prompt set.
- Week 1: smoke + SOC2 evidence exchange.
- Week 2: regression tests + qualitative review with product/clinical SMEs.
- Week 3: load + stability.
- Week 4: final readout + go/no-go decision.

Open items for Medisphere to confirm:
1) Final sample data export (PHI-scrubbed or TEF)?
2) Procurement timeline and PO window (what's your preferred cadence to finalize cost?)
3) Any additional acceptance tests (edge-case safety, latency SLOs per region)?

Ben/Marissa — tagging you for procurement + support commitments and any notes to include in the MAP workbook.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_pathfinder_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Elena Soto <elena@medisphere.com>

Cc: Tim Parks <tim.parks@medisphere.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Pathfinder MAP — success criteria, exit gates & eval tests

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: we'll provide a de-identified sample export (TEF) by EOD Wed 5/26. That has full headers and structure your team needs.
2) Procurement: our procurement lead Tim is cc'd. Target is to have an evaluation contract + PO in place within two weeks of kickoff (so we can cover the month). Any standard short-term eval agreement you use?
3) Clinical acceptance: our quality team will prioritize 10 representative patient scenarios for week 2 review; can we add a qualitative rubric column in the MAP workbook?

Also: for security, our InfoSec would like a copy of your SOC2 summary and a short list of logs/retention options (they typically ask for 90/180/365 day options).

If timeline stays as-is we're happy to kick next Monday 5/31.

Elena
Senior Director, Digital Ops
Medisphere Health

Subject: RE: Mutual Pathfinder MAP — success criteria, exit gates & eval tests

Elena/Tim — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and finalizing acceptance tests in the MAP workbook (attached again):

1) Kickoff: Mon 5/31 — access + sample data ingestion.
2) Week 1: smoke + SOC2 evidence shared (Ben to lead).
3) Week 2: regression pass/fail matrix completed (Medisphere quality rubric column added).
4) Week 3: load test + contingency cycle window.
5) Week 4: final demo + decision meeting (go/no-go) — we'll deliver a concise readout deck and the raw test artifacts.

Acceptance gating rules (short version):
- Must pass at least 3 of 4 quantitative gates (latency, throughput, quality, error rate) AND have no open critical security gaps.
- Any single critical failure (e.g., >5% error rate, data handling non-conformance) triggers an immediate mitigation cycle; if unresolved after two cycles, the eval is paused and an interim review is required.

Elena — Tim, Ben will send the procurement SOW and SOC2 packet today. If you confirm kickoff 5/31 we will lock calendar invites and set up the daily check channel.

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
